source_title: Neuronal physiology of amygdala neurons in the context of injury and pain
node_relevance_reason: Directly describes NPY-containing neurogliaform cells as 14–15% of BLA GABAergic neurons, along with calbindin dendrite-targeting cells (CB+), PV+ basket cells, and SST+ dendrite-targeting cells, with quantitative proportions — highly relevant to bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell and bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron.
summary: A recent immunohistochemical study in mice quantified BLA GABAergic interneuron subtypes: axo-axonic cells 5.5–6%, PV+ basket cells 17–20%, CCK+ cells 7–9%, SST+ dendrite-targeting cells 10–16%, NPY-containing neurogliaform cells 14–15%, VIP/calretinin interneuron-selective interneurons 29–38%, and GABAergic projection neurons co-expressing SST and nNOS 5.5–8% (citing Vereczki et al. 2021). The review also classifies LA-BLA interneurons into four physiological classes: axo-axonic, CB+ dendrite-targeting, AStria, and PV+ basket cells, based on axonal target and firing properties.
quotes: NPY-containing neurogliaform cells are 14–15 %
somatostatin (SST)-expressing dendrite-targeting inhibitory cells are 10–16 %

This categorization resulted in four classes of LA-BLA interneurons: axo-axonic, CB+ (calbindin-positive) dendrite-targeting, AStria (amygdalo-striatal transition area), and PV+ (parvalbumin-positive).

source_title: Transcriptomic diversity of amygdalar subdivisions across humans and nonhuman primates
node_relevance_reason: Identifies 19 transcriptionally distinct inhibitory neuron types in the primate amygdala including SST+, PVALB+, CCK+, VIP+, LAMP5+ and LGE-derived CeA types; reports NPY as top conserved marker for BA-enriched SST_TMEM132C neurons; links CALB1 to PVALB+ subtype diversity; identifies TSHZ1+/FOXP2+ intercalated cells with aspiny morphology — relevant to bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell, bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron, and cea_large_aspiny_neuron/cea_small_aspiny_neuron.
summary: snRNA-seq of five amygdala subdivisions across macaques, baboons, and humans identified 19 inhibitory neuron types: seven CGE-derived (CCK, VIP, LAMP5), seven MGE-derived (SST, PVALB), and five LGE-derived (CeA markers PRKCD and DLK1, plus ITC marker TSHZ1). NPY was the top cross-species conserved marker gene for BA-enriched SST_TMEM132C neurons, while CALB1 distinguishes PVALB+ subtypes. TSHZ1+ ITC populations showed two distinct clusters with spiny and aspiny morphology. MGE- and CGE-derived interneurons were enriched in BLA, while LGE-derived neurons were enriched in CeA.
quotes: For SST+ populations, we found that NPY was the top conserved marker gene for BA-enriched SST_TMEM132C neurons

source_title: Persistent pain intensifies recall of consolidated fear memories
node_relevance_reason: Directly immunostains BLA for calbindin, parvalbumin, somatostatin, and NPY interneuron markers; finds parvalbumin but not calbindin or NPY cell numbers differ with neuropathic pain; also discusses BLA 'fear neurons' and 'extinction neurons' as functionally distinct populations — relevant to bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell, bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron, basal_amygdala_fear_neuron, and basal_amygdala_extinction_neuron.
summary: Immunostaining of BLA for GABA, calbindin, parvalbumin, somatostatin, and NPY markers in mice with and without neuropathic pain found that parvalbumin-positive neuron numbers increased with pain (23±2 vs 35±3), but calbindin-positive neurons were unchanged (~77–78 cells). Almost all PV neurons also co-expressed calbindin. The study also discusses that BLA projection neurons are categorized as 'fear neurons' and 'extinction neurons' based on activity timing relative to the CS, overlapping with PL- and IL-projecting subtypes respectively.
quotes: We immunostained brain sections for a variety of inhibitory neuron markers (GABA, calbindin, parvalbumin, somatostatin, NPY) and compared their expression between mice with and without nerve cuff induced neuropathic pain.
Almost all of these Parv-ir neurons also contained Calb-ir, but the two groups of mice showed the same average number of Calb-ir positive neurons in the BLA

source_title: Facilitation of Contextual Fear Extinction by Orexin-1 Receptor Antagonism Is Associated with the Activation of Specific Amygdala Cell Subpopulations
node_relevance_reason: Directly shows calbindin+ but not parvalbumin+ GABAergic BLA interneurons are activated during fear extinction after OX1R antagonism; defines fear neurons and extinction neurons as overlapping with PL- and IL-projecting BLA populations respectively — directly relevant to bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron, basal_amygdala_fear_neuron, and basal_amygdala_extinction_neuron.
summary: Using retrograde tracing and immunofluorescence, orexin-1 receptor antagonism (SB334867) during contextual fear extinction increased activation of IL-projecting (but not PL-projecting) BLA neurons, consistent with extinction-promoting circuitry. Specifically, calbindin-only+ (CB+PV-) GABAergic interneurons showed increased c-Fos expression, while PV+ and CB+PV+ neurons were unaffected. This identifies calbindin+ BLA interneurons as a distinct subtype activated during fear extinction consolidation.
quotes: GABAergic interneurons expressing calbindin, but not parvalbumin, were also activated by orexin-1 receptor antagonism in the basolateral amygdala.

Distinct populations of BLA neurons encode fear conditioning and extinction processes (Herry et al., 2008). These cell populations, functionally defined as "fear neurons" and "extinction neurons," overlap with 2 different anatomically defined subtypes of BLA neurons projecting to prelimbic medial prefrontal cortex (PL) or IL, respectively
mice treated with SB334867 displayed higher expression of c-Fos within those nonpyramidal neurons containing CB only compared with control animals (P<.01)

source_title: Immature excitatory neurons in the amygdala come of age during puberty
node_relevance_reason: Directly describes the paralaminar nucleus (PL) immature excitatory neuron population, their markers (DCX, PSA-NCAM/Psa-Ncam, BCL-2, TBR1), their protracted maturation from childhood through puberty, their proximity to the lateral ventricle SVZ, and possible migration into neighboring amygdala subnuclei — directly relevant to paralaminar_immature_neuron.
summary: The paralaminar nucleus (PL) of the amygdala contains a large population of immature excitatory neurons expressing DCX and PSA-NCAM that persist from birth through childhood and adolescence on a protracted maturation timeline. At 13 years of age, ~54% of immature DCX+ cells express TBR1 (excitatory neuron transcription factor); mature NEUN+TBR1+ neurons express VGLUT2; only ~3% of PL cells express GAD67 or other interneuron markers (SST, nNOS, CR). The ventral PL comes in close proximity to the ventricular-subventricular zone (V-SVZ) of the temporal lateral ventricle, consistent with a migratory stream origin.
quotes: The PL contains a large population of immature excitatory neurons at birth, some of which may continue to be born from local progenitors. These progenitors disappear rapidly in infancy, but the immature neurons persist throughout childhood and adolescent ages
At 13 years of age, 54.4% of immature DCX+ cells express T-box brain 1 (TBR1), an excitatory neuron transcription factor important for cortical excitatory neuron development

source_title: Molecular characterization of Thy1 expressing fear-inhibiting neurons within the basolateral amygdala
node_relevance_reason: Identifies Ntsr2 as a top upregulated gene in Thy1+ fear-inhibiting BLA neurons by RNA-seq/FACS, characterizes these cells as a 'Fear-Off' population, and proposes NTSR2 supports fear inhibition while NTSR1 supports fear expression — directly relevant to basal_amygdala_extinction_neuron (Ntsr2 marker) and basal_amygdala_fear_neuron.
summary: Thy1-eYFP, Thy1-eNpHR, and Thy1-Cre-labeled BLA neurons consistently act as fear-inhibiting ('Fear-Off') neurons in vivo. RNA sequencing of FACS-sorted Thy1-eYFP neurons identified Ntsr2, Dkk3, Rspo2, and Wnt7a as strongly upregulated genes. Pharmacological manipulation of neurotensin receptor 2 (NTSR2) confirmed the behavioral fear-suppressing effects. The authors propose that NTSR2 supports fear inhibition and NTSR1 supports fear expression, with these populations potentially corresponding to IL/PL-projecting subsets.
quotes: RNA sequencing identifies genes strongly upregulated in RNA of this population, including Ntsr2, Dkk3, Rspo2 and Wnt7a.
These experiments identify and validate Ntsr2-expressing neurons within the BLA, as a putative 'Fear-Off' population.
we propose that NTSR1 supports fear expression and NTSR2 supports fear inhibition via their differential expression within the BLA

source_title: Neuronal types in the mouse amygdala and their transcriptional response to fear conditioning
node_relevance_reason: Comprehensive scRNA-seq taxonomy of the mouse amygdala identifying 56 GABAergic clusters (13,006 cells) and 130 neuronal types total; canonical interneurons (GABA-35 to GABA-56 expressing Sst, Pvalb, Vip, Sncg) are BLA-restricted and make up 59% of BLA neurons; CeA types include multiple Ppp1r1b+ MSN-like subtypes — relevant to bla_npy_neurogliaform_cell, bla_calbindin_dendrite_targeting_interneuron, cea_large_aspiny_neuron, and cea_small_aspiny_neuron.
summary: Whole-cell scRNA-seq of the adult mouse amygdala (30,184 neurons, 130 types) reveals amygdala inhibitory cell types split into projecting MSN-like types (IA/CEA) and local interneurons. Canonical MGE/CGE-derived interneurons (Sst, Pvalb, Vip, Sncg) expressing local-marker genes Nfib/Nfix/Tcf4/Satb1/Prox1 are designated GABA-35 to GABA-56, predominantly located in the BLA, and constitute 59% of BLA neurons. CEA types (GABA-5 to GABA-21) express Ppp1r1b (DARPP-32) and markers of MSN-like projecting neurons. Two Pvalb+ interneuron populations (GABA-41, GABA-44) have similar spatial distributions in BLA but divergent CFC transcriptional responses.
quotes: canonical interneurons GABA-35 to GABA-56, which make up just 59% of neurons in mouse BLA

Local/interneuron markers Nfib, Nfix, Tcf4, Satb1 and Prox1 (ref. 30) were expressed among canonical medial ganglionic eminences (MGE)- and caudal ganglionic eminences (CGE)-derived interneuron types (for example, Sst, Pvalb, Vip or Sncg) of the Maf/Zeb2 branch

source_title: The role of inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate 3-kinase A in regulating emotional behavior and amygdala function
node_relevance_reason: Confirms CeA GABAergic interneurons as the primary cell type expressing IP3K-A; discusses neuropeptide Y as a GPCR ligand in amygdala circuits; identifies CeA as primarily GABAergic — provides context for cea_large_aspiny_neuron and cea_small_aspiny_neuron but no direct morphological data on aspiny subtypes.
summary: IP3K-A is highly enriched in CeA GABAergic neurons (colocalizing with GAD67) and in BLA CaMKII-positive excitatory pyramidal neurons. The study discusses neuropeptide Y (NPY), cholecystokinin, and corticotrophin-releasing hormone as GPCR ligands integrating CeA circuit activity. Loss of IP3K-A altered amygdala gene expression, reducing c-Fos in both BLA and CeA, suggesting IP3K-A modulates excitatory-inhibitory circuit balance.
quotes: In the CeA, IP3K-A primarily colocalized with GAD67-positive GABAergic interneurons, whereas most IP3K-A in the BLA was in CAMKIIα-positive excitatory pyramidal neurons
